item.title: General Assembly approves medical marijuana vaping, removes THC limits - The Current
item.description: The Georgia General Assembly passed a bill to lift the limit on THC content in medical marijuana and allow registered patients to vape the drug, providing faster relief, with the bill now awaiting Gov. Brian Kemp's signature.

item.title: Lawmakers may restrict access to police video, mugshots in Georgia - The Current
item.description: Senate Bill 482 in Georgia aims to protect victims of tragedies from exploitative websites, but free speech advocates argue it could disadvantage some news outlets by requiring in-person and notarized requests for booking photos and videos, as well as court orders for media of dead or dying people.

item.title: Environmental groups sue over Georgia Power’s energy expansion for data centers - The Current
item.description: A group of environmental organizations filed a lawsuit against the Georgia Public Service Commission, alleging that the commission broke the law by approving nearly 10 gigawatts of new energy generation without properly demonstrating a need for it, which the lawsuit argues will leave customers on the hook for an estimated $50 to $60 billion in costs over the coming decades.

item.title: Georgia politics: Special elections, departures shape political landscape - The Current
item.description: Georgia lawmakers are rushing to pass bills before the end of the session, while election season is heating up with debates and special elections, and some lawmakers are choosing to step down from their positions.

item.title: Georgia Senate cuts $110M from public college funding in $38.5B budget - The Current
item.description: The Georgia Senate passed its version of the $38.5 billion FY2027 budget, which included reduced funding for public colleges and universities, increased funding for private K-12 school vouchers, and added funding for the state employee pension system, and was sent to the House for negotiations.

item.title: Georgia Senate votes for rapid move to hand-marked paper ballots before November elections - The Current
item.description: The Georgia Senate passed a bill that would switch the state's voting system to hand-marked paper ballots, setting up a showdown with the House over a competing bill that would delay the transition until 2028.

item.title: GOP measure to cap out-of-state campaign donations advancing through Georgia House - The Current
item.description: Senate Bill 423, which would make it a felony for an intermediary to send money from out-of-state donors and give it to a local campaign, passed a state House committee and is nearing final passage in the final days of this year's legislative session.

item.title: The Current GA and ProPublica project earns national recognition from SABEW - The Current
item.description: The Current GA, in collaboration with ProPublica, received an Honorable Mention in the Best in Business Awards for their reporting on Georgia's Medicaid work requirement program, which highlighted systemic issues affecting low-income Georgians.

item.title: Bill creating standards for community health workers in Georgia has stalled - The Current
item.description: House Bill 291, which would mandate criminal background checks and set up standards for educating and certifying community health workers, passed the House and Senate Health and Human Services Committee, but was not chosen by the Senate Rules Committee to reach the Senate floor for a full vote before the session ended.

item.title: Georgia lawmakers went after corporate landlords. They did not get far - The Current
item.description: In a rare bipartisan moment, the Georgia state Senate passed a bill to punish institutional investors with more than 500 single-family rental homes, but the bill was later replaced with another measure in the House.
